summary: Shigeru Kato worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from circa 1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1957) and Harvard University (~1963–1967). He held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1968–1998) and Tenri University, and he taught Yoshitsugu Sawai.
Shih-Hsiang Chen worked in sinology. He studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1945–1971), where he taught Gary Snyder.

Shikaripur N. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. His career includes posts at Stony Brook University, serving as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and held a post at Bukkyo University from circa 1970 to 1977.

Shikha Rajpurohit is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied Sanskrit at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (2009–2012) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (2014–2022), later becoming an assistant professor at Krea University in 2024.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Boone University, Peking University, and Zhejiang University, and taught Chun-i Tang, Zongsan Mou, and Fuguan Xu.

Shilpa Sumant is an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2000–2007). She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2009 and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 2020 to 2025.

Shimei Futabatei studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. In addition to teaching Haya Akegarasu, he held posts at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, Naval War College, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, and Osaka Asahi Shimbun.

Shimin Geng specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from circa 1949 to 1953 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested in 1991, and as associate professor in 2000) and Hiroshima University (attested 1992).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Harvard universities, and taught Masaaki Hattori, Masao Abe, Seikaku Hirata, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Seizan Yanagida.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and founded Kindai Pyramido Kyokai. He held a post as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).

Shin'ya Yasutomi studied at Waseda University and Otani University, earning a doctorate. He served as a professor at Otani University (2014) and held posts at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute (~2011–2017) and Eastern Buddhist Society.
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1952–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1983).

Shindo Kusumoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura. Kusumoto also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Tohoku and Rissho universities under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He held posts at Koyasan University as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He taught Kei Kataoka and held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology, the University of Tokyo, and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Shinichi Nakazawa is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977). He has held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned a Ph.D. at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Eastern Institute, and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
